evidence.evidence_paraphrase: AuNR/Ag nanostructures produced a 129-fold SERS enhancement relative to pure AuNRs when decorated with 4MBA, supporting Ag-associated plasmonic enhancement.
The authors observed AuNR/Ag agglomeration on cell membranes, associated with increased SERS intensity, and reported preliminary nonlinear correlations between signal intensity and cluster size.
The reported nanorods were silver-coated AuNRs functionalized with Raman molecules and antibodies; the methods do not describe polymer-defined, varied Ag bridge gaps.

assessments.scientific_rationale: The paper supports Ag-mediated SERS enhancement and reports that AuNR/Ag agglomeration increases SERS intensity with a nonlinear dependence on cluster size. However, it does not test controlled variation of a polymer-defined inner/outer Ag gap in an Ag-bridge architecture or establish a reproducible directional gap-size trend under matched conditions.

evidence.evidence_paraphrase: SERS was compared for 4MBA in solution and after deposition on AuNRs or AuNR/Ag, but this is not a paired dispersed-versus-dried measurement of the same analyte-mixed preparation.
AuNR/Ag agglomeration on cell membranes was reported to increase SERS intensity, with a preliminary nonlinear signal relationship to cluster size.
For the targeting assay, samples were fixed, washed, left to dry, and then subjected to Raman measurement; no corresponding pre-drying measurement is described.

assessments.scientific_rationale: The paper provides related context-dependent SERS evidence: Ag-coated nanorods show enhanced signal, and cellular agglomeration is associated with increased intensity. It does not perform a paired solution-to-dried comparison of the same analyte-mixed preparation, nor does it establish a normalized peak-intensity distribution or qualitative peak-profile transformation across that transition.
